name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Pret. It’s the fastest way to fix formatting drift without touching logic, so it won’t break builds or introduce bugs. The trade-off is that we accept upstream drift may reoccur, but the cost of manual fixes outweighs the risk of occasional re-patching.

name: Gauge
text: Auto-applying whitespace patches risks breaking tooling that depends on exact formatting—like Pret’s own dry-run misreading indentation that *matters* in Python. A safer alternative is to fork the dependency, apply fixes there, and vendor it; this isolates changes from upstream drift and makes the fix auditable. Settle it by testing the patched dependency in CI with the full toolchain before committing.
